To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the E. coli replication protein DnaC exists in two conformers with different nucleotide-binding capabilities, (ii) ATP and ADP binding to DnaC occurs in a two-step sequential mechanism, and (iii) DnaC binding to the nucleotides is accompanied by large changes in their environment, which are reflected in the fluorescence intensity of the cofactors.
(1) ATP binds to the (C)(2)(DnaC) conformation of DnaC protein and (2) ATP binding to (C)(1)(DnaC), the conformational state that binds ATP, is not possible.

(1) the DnaC conformational equilibrium shifts in the presence of nucleotides toward the state that binds the cofactor, (2) the binding mechanism is sequential, and (3) only one protein conformation binds nucleotide cofactors, while the other conformation does not bind the cofactor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of the nucleoside triphosphate binding to DnaC protein and its role in DNA replication.
the mechanism of ATP and ADPNP binding to DnaC protein.
the mechanism of the nucleic acid synthesis in prokaryotes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of ATP and/or ADP fluorescent analogs to the DnaC replicative factor is a sequential two-step process that includes the formation of the DnaG-DnaC complex, followed by the binding of the nucleotide cofactors.
the DnaC is an ATPase, which is a member of the AAA+ family of proteins, that is capable of hydrolyzing ATP and ADP with the same efficiency and the same mechanism.
the DnaC conformational equilibrium is shifted in favor of the (C)(2)-state in the presence of ATP or ADP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DnaC conformational equilibrium is a prerequisite for the DnaC-ATP binding, and that the DnaB helicase binding to the DnaC-DnaB complex is accompanied by a conformational change of the complex that shifts the equilibrium of the DnaB-DnaC complex toward the (DnaB)(2)-(DnaC)(0) state.
the DnaC is a protein which exists in two conformers, one of them being the active one.
DnaC exists in two conformers, (DnaC), and (DnaC)2, and that the nucleotide binding site is open in the (DnaCl) conformation and closed in the (DncC)2 conformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleotide-binding domain of the Dna C protein is in a conformation that does not permit the binding of the nucleotide.

the DnaC ATPase activity is a consequence of the equilibrium of the protein between two conformations with distinct ATP binding capabilities, and that the ATP hydrolysis activity is not an intrinsic property of the Dna protein.

DnaC protein can be in two different conformations, and that the binding of ATP or ADP analogues to DnaC protein involves a protein conformational change, and that the conformation of DnaC protein in the presence of ATP is shifted toward the (C)(2), the ATP-binding state, and that the ATP binding to (C)(1), the non-ATP-binding state is prevented by a stringent locking mechanism.
